classification.difficultyReason: Constructs a diagram from two bearings, identifies the smaller included angle across north, obtains an exact distance, then converts a calculated triangle angle into the correctly oriented bearing.

content.prompt: From a lighthouse $L$, a ship $S$ bears $51^\circ30'\mathrm{T}$ and is at a distance of $8$ km. From $L$ a boat $B$ bears $291^\circ30'\mathrm{T}$ and is at a distance of $6$ km.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a clear diagram marking on it the information supplied.

answer.short: Diagram showing $LS=8$ km on bearing $051^\circ30'\mathrm{T}$ and $LB=6$ km on bearing $291^\circ30'\mathrm{T}$.
answer.worked: Draw a north reference at $L$. Measure both bearings clockwise from north, then label $L$, $S$, $B$ and the two distances.

spec.description: Bearing diagram derived from the supplied distances and bearings; ordinary marks are black and no fill is used.
spec.mathematics: Offsets from L are (8 sin 51.5°,8 cos 51.5°) and (6 sin 291.5°,6 cos 291.5°). Both bearing arcs run clockwise from north, including the reflex bearing to B.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the distance of ship $S$ from boat $B$. Give your answer as a surd.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the bearing of the ship $S$ from boat $B$. Give your answer to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
The bearing of $L$ from $B$ is $111^\circ30'\mathrm{T}$. Let $\theta=\angle LBS$.

$$\begin{align*}\cos\theta&=\frac{6^2+(2\sqrt{37})^2-8^2}{2(6)(2\sqrt{37})}\\\cos\theta&=\frac{5}{\sqrt{37}}\\\theta&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{\sqrt{37}}\right)\end{align*}$$

The line $BS$ lies north of $BL$, so subtract this angle from the bearing of $L$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing of }S\text{ from }B&=111.5^\circ-\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{\sqrt{37}}\right)\\\text{Bearing of }S\text{ from }B&\approx76.78^\circ\end{align*}$$

To the nearest degree, the bearing is $077^\circ\mathrm{T}$.
